Formulation  
Predisposing: Family history of autoimmune illness (father); high work demands.  
Precipitating: Recent viral illness; increased physical strain from boxing classes; acute neurological symptoms.  
Perpetuating: Ongoing numbness/tingling; uncertainty regarding diagnosis; health-related anxiety.  
Protective: Active help-seeking; exercise routine; social connections; good insight.  

Mental Health Care Plan Details  

Principal Problem: Health-related anxiety secondary to unexplained neurological symptoms  
- Patient Goal(s): Understand and manage worry while awaiting neurological work-up  
- Clinical Goal(s): Reduce anxiety; ensure adequate coping strategies during diagnostic process  
- Actions (Patient):  
  • Utilize coping techniques (relaxation, scheduled worry time)  
  • Maintain regular sleep and exercise as tolerated  
  • Monitor anxiety levels; seek help if symptoms escalate  
- Actions (Clinician/GP):  
  • Provide clear information about referral process and likely timelines  
  • Offer brief supportive counseling; consider short psychoeducation session on health anxiety  
  • Reassess mental health at follow-up or sooner if patient reports increased distress  

Secondary Problem: Fatigue and disrupted sleep routine  
- Patient Goal(s): Improve energy levels and sleep quality  
- Clinical Goal(s): Identify contributing factors (anxiety, over-exercise, possible neurological etiology); promote sleep hygiene  
- Actions (Patient):  
  • Implement sleep-hygiene strategies; limit late-night screen time  
  • Moderate exercise intensity pending neurology advice  
- Actions (Clinician/GP):  
  • Review melatonin use; ensure appropriate dosing and timing  
  • Assess iron supplementation adherence; arrange labs if indicated  
  • Discuss pacing of activities until diagnosis clarified  

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention  
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Nature of possible neurological conditions (e.g., MS), red-flag symptoms needing ED assessment (progressive weakness, headaches, vomiting, seizures, worsening vision)  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increased limb weakness, new visual changes, escalating anxiety, insomnia  
- Coping Strategies: Relaxation techniques, maintaining routine, seeking social support, prompt medical review if red-flag symptoms appear

- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: None currently

- Review Date: To be scheduled after neurology appointment or within 4 weeks, whichever is sooner
